Research.title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation
Research.summary: This paper highlights a critical methodological flaw in LLM evaluation: using a single overall accuracy or F1 score to validate an automatic scorer can mask differential error rates across conditions being compared, leading to biased conclusions about model behavior. For teams building evaluation pipelines for conversational AI, this is a practical reminder to validate scorers separately across each experimental condition rather than in aggregate. The finding is directly applicable to anyone running A/B tests on prompt variants or measuring LLM susceptibility to conversational pressure.

Research.title: MisconceptDialogue: Evaluation Criteria Shape Measured Success in LLM Math Tutoring
Research.summary: MISCONCEPTDIALOGUE is a fully automated framework that benchmarks LLMs (7B–14B) as math tutors across error detection, misconception diagnosis, and multi-turn remediation, while also exposing how choice of evaluation metric dramatically changes which model appears best. Practitioners building AI tutoring or educational products should note that reported benchmark numbers are highly sensitive to evaluation design, and that the full tutoring pipeline—not just single-turn accuracy—must be assessed end-to-end. The automated LLM-simulated student approach also offers a reusable scaffold for testing dialogue agents in other domains.
affiliations: Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute, Republic of Korea
Department of Artificial Intelligence, University of Science and Technology, Republic of Korea

Research.title: Knowledge Graphs Quality Assessment in the Era of LLMs: A Conceptual Framework
Research.summary: This paper surveys KG quality dimensions—completeness, accuracy, freshness, and traceability—specifically in the context of using KGs as grounding sources for LLMs and RAG systems. It provides a conceptual framework for deciding when a KG is trustworthy enough to ground an LLM response, which is practically relevant for teams building enterprise RAG or knowledge-backed agents. The work surfaces underappreciated risks of low-quality KGs silently degrading LLM output reliability.
affiliations: Institute for Technology and Humanity, University of Cambridge, UK

Research.title: AI Is Getting Good at Math. Here's Why.
Research.summary: This analysis identifies an emerging pattern in which AI models are systematically conquering mathematical problem classes, with the trajectory suggesting predictable frontiers for near-term capability gains. For product builders, understanding which mathematical reasoning capabilities are maturing—and in what order—is valuable for timing applications in scientific computing, code generation, and quantitative reasoning. The piece also explores the structural reasons (training signal quality, verifiability) behind math being a leading domain for AI progress.

Tools.title: Does Your Model Run on AWS Trainium? Look It Up
Tools.summary: Hugging Face has launched a lookup resource for checking which models are supported on AWS Trainium via the torch-neuronx stack, reducing the friction of validating hardware compatibility before committing to AWS's custom AI accelerators. This is immediately useful for teams evaluating Trainium as a cost-effective alternative to GPU instances for inference or fine-tuning workloads. The tool complements the broader push toward diversifying away from NVIDIA hardware.

Tools.title: LitPivot: Developing research ideas through dynamic contextualization within the literature landscape
Tools.summary: AllenAI's LitPivot is a tool that helps researchers dynamically navigate and recontextualize ideas within the scientific literature landscape, surfacing relevant adjacent work to accelerate hypothesis generation. For AI product teams doing competitive research or tracking fast-moving fields, this kind of literature-aware ideation tool could reduce the overhead of staying current. It reflects a broader trend of agentic research assistants built on top of semantic scholar-scale paper corpora.

Industry News.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?
Industry News.summary: A detailed analysis explores the competitive and structural dynamics behind dramatic price cuts from OpenAI and Anthropic, pointing to factors including inference efficiency gains, increased competition from open-weight models, and a race for market share over margins. For AI product builders, the price drops substantially change the economics of LLM-powered features and may accelerate build-vs-buy decisions. The piece is essential reading for anyone modeling the cost structure of AI applications.

Industry News.title: Kimi 3.1 Pro 104BA-2.8T: Fable-5.1-Class Open Weights narrows Closed-AI lead to ~1 month
Industry News.summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi 3.1 Pro, a 104B active / 2.8T parameter MoE model, achieves performance competitive with leading closed frontier models and ships with a 2–3× faster Pro Highspeed API tier. The open-weights release signals that the gap between open and closed frontier models has compressed to roughly one month of capability lag, which has significant implications for enterprise deployments that require on-premise or customizable models. Teams evaluating open-weight alternatives to GPT or Claude-class models should benchmark Kimi 3.1 Pro immediately.

Industry News.title: Apollo says AI has delivered 'zero financial payoff' outside the tech industry
Industry News.summary: Apollo Global's economic analysis finds no measurable financial return from AI adoption in non-tech corporate America, despite significant investment, suggesting the productivity gains widely anticipated have yet to materialize at scale. This is a sobering data point for consultants and product teams pitching AI ROI to non-tech enterprises, and may accelerate scrutiny of AI spending by CFOs heading into 2027 planning cycles. It also raises questions about whether current AI products are well-suited to the workflows and constraints of traditional industries.

Industry News.title: Microsoft Decision-1: 9B Qwen Model Launch Explained
Industry News.summary: Microsoft has launched Decision-1, a 9B-parameter model based on the Qwen3.5 architecture, positioned for decision-making and agentic task workloads. The release continues Microsoft's pattern of fine-tuning and deploying open-weight base models under its own brand for Azure customers, giving enterprise teams a supported, cloud-native option for smaller reasoning-capable models. The 9B scale targets cost-sensitive deployments where a full frontier model is unnecessary.
